scope_note:
This domain covers vehicle and roadside fire emergencies only.
Medical treatment of burns is cross-referenced to DOMAIN-003 (First Aid).
Crash-scene hazard assessment is cross-referenced to DOMAIN-001 (Road
Accident). Mechanical breakdown symptoms are cross-referenced to DOMAIN-004
(Vehicle Breakdown).

knowledge_records.topic: Early warning signs of a vehicle fire
knowledge_records.title: Treat smoke or a burning smell as a possible vehicle fire
knowledge_records.content:
Smoke from the bonnet, dashboard, wheel area, or passenger cabin, or a
strong smell of burning rubber, plastic, oil, petrol, or wiring, should be treated as a
possible developing vehicle fire. The safe response is to stop as soon as it is safe,
switch off the vehicle, and evacuate occupants rather than continuing to drive.
safe_actions: Treat smoke, burning smell, or unexplained heat as a possible fire.
Stop the vehicle as soon as it is safe.
Switch off the engine and electrical systems.
Get all occupants out of the vehicle.
Move away from the vehicle and contact emergency services.
unsafe_actions: Do not keep driving in the hope of reaching a workshop or fuel station.
Do not remain inside the vehicle while trying to identify the source of the smell.
escalation_criteria: Unusual heat from the cabin, floor, bonnet, or dashboard

knowledge_records.topic: Early warning signs of a vehicle fire
knowledge_records.title: Repeated electrical faults or sparks can indicate a developing fire
knowledge_records.content:
Repeated electrical failure, blown fuses, flickering lights, visible sparks or
arcing, and unusual heat through the floor, pedals, or dashboard can indicate a
developing vehicle fire and justify immediate safe stopping and evacuation.
safe_actions: Stop the vehicle safely when repeated electrical faults or sparks appear.
Switch off the ignition and evacuate occupants.
Report electrical symptoms to emergency responders.
unsafe_actions: Do not ignore repeated electrical faults, sparking, or a burning-plastic smell.
Do not continue using electrical accessories after these signs appear.
escalation_criteria: Heat radiating through the dashboard or floor

knowledge_records.topic: Immediate actions when a vehicle catches fire while driving
knowledge_records.title: Stop, switch off, evacuate, and move away
knowledge_records.content:
If a vehicle catches fire or produces heavy smoke while driving, the
emergency sequence is to pull over safely, switch off the engine and ignition, apply
the parking brake, evacuate everyone immediately, move far away from the vehicle,
and call the fire service or integrated emergency number.
safe_actions: Indicate and pull over to the left shoulder or nearest safe stopping point.
Switch off the engine and ignition.
Apply the parking brake.
Release locking and evacuate all occupants immediately.
Move upwind and away from the vehicle.
Call emergency services from a safe distance.
unsafe_actions: Do not continue driving with a burning or heavily smoking vehicle.
Do not delay evacuation while attempting repairs or filming the fire.
escalation_criteria: Fire near fuel tank, fuel lines, or gas cylinder

knowledge_records.topic: Immediate actions when a vehicle catches fire while driving
knowledge_records.title:
Do not stop next to fuel stations, gas installations, dry grass, or other vehicles
if avoidable
knowledge_records.content:
When pulling over with a burning or heavily smoking vehicle, avoid
stopping next to a fuel station, gas installation, dry vegetation, or another vehicle if it
can be avoided, because the fire can spread or trigger secondary hazards.
safe_actions: Choose the safest available stopping point away from secondary fire hazards.
unsafe_actions:
Do not stop next to a fuel station, gas installation, dry vegetation, or another vehicle
if a safer alternative is available.
escalation_criteria: Vehicle is smoking or on fire near other flammable hazards

knowledge_records.topic: Safe evacuation of occupants
knowledge_records.title: Evacuate all occupants immediately and account for everyone
knowledge_records.content:
Every occupant must leave a burning vehicle immediately. Children,
elderly passengers, and people with reduced mobility should be helped out directly,
and a headcount should be done once everyone is outside to confirm that no one
remains in the vehicle.
safe_actions: Release seatbelts and child restraints immediately.
Assist children, elderly passengers, and persons with disability first.
Do a headcount once outside.
Move everyone together to a single safe point away from the vehicle.
unsafe_actions: Do not leave any occupant inside while assessing the fire.
Do not assume everyone has exited without checking.

knowledge_records.topic: Safe evacuation of occupants
knowledge_records.title: Use the side away from traffic if possible
knowledge_records.content:
When evacuating a burning or smoking vehicle, occupants should exit
through doors on the side away from moving traffic where possible, to reduce the
risk of being struck by passing vehicles.
safe_actions: Use doors on the non-traffic side where possible.
Check for moving traffic before stepping out.
unsafe_actions: Do not step directly into a live traffic lane without checking.
escalation_criteria: Fire on a high-speed road or narrow shoulder

knowledge_records.topic: Safe evacuation of occupants
knowledge_records.title: Do not re-enter for pets, luggage, or belongings
knowledge_records.content:
Once a fire has started, no occupant should re-enter the vehicle to
retrieve pets, luggage, or belongings, because smoke becomes disabling quickly and
the fire can spread rapidly into the cabin.
safe_actions: Keep all occupants together at a safe point away from the vehicle.
Wait for professional responders.
unsafe_actions: Do not re-enter the vehicle for pets, luggage, or belongings.
escalation_criteria: Any person attempting to return to the vehicle after evacuation

knowledge_records.topic: Safe distance and perimeter management
knowledge_records.title: Move at least 30 metres away from a burning conventional vehicle
knowledge_records.content:
A burning conventional vehicle can produce flying debris, bursting tyres,
exploding gas struts, and intense toxic smoke. A practical public-safety rule is to
move at least 30 metres away from a burning petrol or diesel vehicle, and further if
the fire grows.
safe_actions: Move at least 30 metres away from the vehicle.
Move further if the fire grows or conditions worsen.
Keep others back from the vehicle.
unsafe_actions: Do not stand close to a burning vehicle.
Do not gather near the fire to watch or record it.
escalation_criteria: Fire spreading to cabin or fuel-tank area
Crowd gathering near the burning vehicle
knowledge_records.notes:
Practical stand-off value; not confirmed as a statutory public distance in the
supplied dataset.

knowledge_records.topic: Safe distance and perimeter management
knowledge_records.title: Move 50 metres or more away from burning CNG, LPG, or electric vehicles
knowledge_records.content:
For a burning CNG, LPG, or electric vehicle, the practical public-safety
rule is to move at least 50 metres away, and further if the fire grows, because gas
cylinders can vent or rupture and high-voltage battery fires can vent flammable
vapour and reignite.
safe_actions: Move at least 50 metres away from a burning CNG, LPG, or electric vehicle.
Increase distance further if the fire grows or cylinders vent.
Keep others away from the hazard zone.
unsafe_actions: Do not stand close to a gas-fuelled or electric vehicle fire.
Do not remain near the vehicle because visible flames appear reduced.
escalation_criteria: Hissing, whistling, or venting from a gas or battery system
Vehicle identified as CNG, LPG, electric, or hybrid
knowledge_records.notes:
Practical stand-off value; not confirmed as a statutory public distance in the
supplied dataset.

knowledge_records.topic: Safe distance and perimeter management
knowledge_records.title: Stand upwind and behind a barrier where possible
knowledge_records.content:
When waiting near a vehicle fire, people should stand upwind so smoke
blows away from them and stay behind a solid barrier such as a crash barrier, wall,
or embankment where one is available.
safe_actions: Stand upwind of the smoke.
Use a crash barrier, wall, or embankment for protection where available.
Keep bystanders back from the scene.
unsafe_actions: Do not stand downwind in the smoke plume.
Do not remain exposed between the fire and moving traffic.

knowledge_records.topic: Safe distance and perimeter management
knowledge_records.title: Do not stand directly in front of or behind a burning vehicle
knowledge_records.content:
People should not stand directly in front of or behind a burning vehicle,
because bursting tyres, gas struts, and other pressurised components may project
outward in those directions.
safe_actions: Move to the side and further away from the vehicle.
Use distance and barriers to protect yourself.
unsafe_actions: Do not stand directly in front of a burning vehicle.
Do not stand directly behind a burning vehicle.
escalation_criteria: Tyres heating, bursting, or visible under-inflation during fire

knowledge_records.topic: When to use and when NOT to use a fire extinguisher
knowledge_records.title: Only a very small, just-started fire may be tackled by an untrained person
knowledge_records.content:
An untrained person may only consider using a portable fire extinguisher
on a vehicle fire when the fire is very small and has just started, everyone is already
out of the vehicle, a suitable extinguisher is immediately available, and there is a
clear escape route behind them.
safe_actions:
Ensure everyone is already out and at a safe distance before considering
extinguisher use.
Use an extinguisher only for a very small, just-started fire.
Keep a clear escape route behind you.
unsafe_actions: Do not fight the fire while occupants are still inside.
Do not attempt extinguisher use without a clear escape route.

knowledge_records.topic: When to use and when NOT to use a fire extinguisher
knowledge_records.title: Never fight a spreading, fuel-fed, gas, or EV battery fire yourself
knowledge_records.content:
A bystander must not attempt to fight a vehicle fire that has spread to the
passenger cabin, involves fuel leakage or fuel-fed flames, involves a CNG or LPG
cylinder, or involves an electric-vehicle battery. In all of these situations, the correct
action is immediate withdrawal and fire-service escalation.
safe_actions: Withdraw to a safe distance.
Call 112 and report the vehicle type and hazard type.
Keep bystanders away from the fire.
unsafe_actions: Do not attempt to fight a cabin fire.
Do not attempt to fight a fuel-fed fire.
Do not attempt to fight a gas-cylinder fire.
Do not attempt to fight an EV battery fire.

knowledge_records.topic: When to use and when NOT to use a fire extinguisher
knowledge_records.title: Abandon extinguishing if the fire does not go out immediately
knowledge_records.content:
If a vehicle fire does not go out immediately with the first extinguisher
discharge, or if smoke thickens or flames grow, the attempt should be abandoned
and the person should withdraw to a safe distance and wait for the fire service.
safe_actions: Withdraw immediately if the fire persists after the first discharge.
Move to a safe distance and wait for responders.
unsafe_actions: Do not continue after the fire grows or the extinguisher is exhausted.
Do not remain between the fire and your only exit route.

knowledge_records.topic: Correct fire extinguisher type and technique
knowledge_records.title: Use a BIS-marked ABC dry powder extinguisher for vehicle use
knowledge_records.content:
A multi-purpose ABC dry chemical powder extinguisher conforming to
Indian Standards is the type most commonly specified for vehicle use in India
because vehicle fires may involve solids, flammable liquids, and live electrical
equipment together.
safe_actions: Use a BIS-marked ABC dry powder extinguisher suitable for vehicle use.
Keep the extinguisher accessible inside the cabin rather than locked in the boot.
Service and refill it as required.
unsafe_actions: Do not rely on an expired, unmarked, discharged, or unsuitable extinguisher.

knowledge_records.topic: Correct fire extinguisher type and technique
knowledge_records.title: Basic extinguisher technique: pull, aim at the base, squeeze, sweep
knowledge_records.content:
The standard technique for a portable extinguisher on a very small
vehicle fire is to pull the safety pin, aim the nozzle at the base of the flames rather
than the flame tips, squeeze the lever, and sweep side to side across the base of the
fire.
safe_actions: Pull the safety pin.
Aim at the base of the fire.
Squeeze the lever.
Sweep side to side across the base of the flames.
unsafe_actions: Do not aim at the top of the flames instead of the base.
escalation_criteria: Fire not controlled immediately after discharge

knowledge_records.topic: Correct fire extinguisher type and technique
knowledge_records.title: Do not use water on fuel or live electrical vehicle fires
knowledge_records.content:
Water must not be used on petrol, diesel, oil, or live electrical vehicle fires
because it can spread burning fuel and creates electrocution risk.
safe_actions: Use only an appropriate extinguisher for a very small fire.
Withdraw and call the fire service for anything larger or riskier.
unsafe_actions: Do not throw water on petrol, diesel, oil, or live electrical fires.

knowledge_records.topic: Danger of opening the bonnet or hood
knowledge_records.title: Do not fully open the bonnet of a burning or heavily smoking vehicle
knowledge_records.content:
Fully opening the bonnet during an engine-compartment fire admits a
rush of oxygen that can cause a sudden flare-up or flashback, and the bonnet, catch,
and nearby metal can be extremely hot. The default safe action is to leave the
bonnet closed, evacuate, and call the fire service.
safe_actions: Leave the bonnet closed.
Evacuate occupants.
Call the fire service.
unsafe_actions: Do not fully open or raise the bonnet of a burning or heavily smoking vehicle.
Do not touch a hot bonnet or catch with bare hands.
escalation_criteria: Smoke or fire in the engine bay

knowledge_records.topic: Danger of opening the bonnet or hood
knowledge_records.title:
Catch-gap extinguisher use is conditional and should not override the
closed-bonnet default
knowledge_records.content:
Some guidance permits releasing the bonnet catch only and discharging
an extinguisher through the narrow gap for a very small engine fire, without raising
the bonnet. Because this sits beside the stronger default instruction to leave the
bonnet closed and call the fire service, it should be treated as conditional rather than
general public advice.
safe_actions: Use the closed-bonnet-and-call-fire-service approach as the default answer.

If this conditional method is ever presented, limit it to a very small fire with a suitable
extinguisher and immediate withdrawal if flames flare.
unsafe_actions:
Do not present conditional catch-gap discharge as the standard response to an
engine fire.
escalation_criteria: Any uncertainty about the size of the fire
Heat or flames already escaping from the bonnet gap
knowledge_records.notes:
Supplied material preserves a conflict between strict closed-bonnet
guidance and a limited catch-gap discharge technique.

knowledge_records.topic: Fuel-related fire and explosion hazards
knowledge_records.title: Petrol vapour can spread along the ground and ignite from a spark
knowledge_records.content:
Petrol vapour is heavier than air, spreads along the ground, and can be
ignited by a spark, hot surface, or cigarette. Any fuel leak at a fire or crash scene
requires immediate withdrawal, ignition-source control, and fire-service escalation.
safe_actions: Move away from the spill and stay upwind and uphill if possible.
Call emergency services and report fuel leakage.
unsafe_actions: Do not smoke or use flame or spark sources near a fuel leak.
Do not walk through pooled fuel.
escalation_criteria: Fuel fire or fuel near heat source

knowledge_records.topic: Fuel-related fire and explosion hazards
knowledge_records.title: Do not restart a fuel-leaking vehicle or create ignition sources nearby
knowledge_records.content:
A vehicle that is leaking fuel should not be restarted, and people should
keep all ignition sources away, including cigarettes, lighters, matches, or hot
equipment. Other vehicles should be prevented from driving through or stopping in
the spill area if it is safe to manage the scene.
safe_actions: Switch off the engine.
Keep other vehicles away from the spill if it is safe to do so.
Report the leak to emergency responders.
unsafe_actions: Do not restart the engine of a vehicle that is leaking fuel.
Do not smoke or use lighters or matches near the leak.
Do not try to wash away or mop up spilled fuel yourself.
escalation_criteria: Fuel spill near a drain, fuel station, or built-up area

cross_domain_escalation.condition: Fuel leakage occurring after a collision with casualties
cross_domain_escalation.action:
Use road-accident casualty and scene-safety guidance alongside fire
guidance.

knowledge_records.topic: Electric vehicle battery fire (thermal runaway)
knowledge_records.title: Recognise thermal runaway signs in an electric vehicle
knowledge_records.content:
Possible lithium-ion battery thermal runaway signs include hissing,
popping, crackling or whistling from under the floor, white or grey vapour venting
from the battery area, rapid heat build-up, or smoke from the underbody after a crash
or charging fault.
safe_actions: Treat these signs as a battery emergency and evacuate immediately.
Move everyone a long distance away and stay upwind.
Call emergency services and state that an electric vehicle battery may be involved.
unsafe_actions: Do not assume the vehicle is safe because there are no visible external flames.
Do not stay close to the underbody area to inspect the battery.
escalation_criteria: Hissing, popping, or whistling from battery area
Heat or smoke after charging or collision
knowledge_records.notes:
International source used because India-specific EV battery fire SOPs are
unresolved in the supplied dataset.

knowledge_records.topic: Electric vehicle battery fire (thermal runaway)
knowledge_records.title:
Do not touch orange cables, the battery pack, or damaged battery
enclosures
knowledge_records.content:
After a crash or fire involving an electric vehicle, no untrained person
should touch orange high-voltage cables, the battery pack, or damaged battery
enclosures because of electric shock, arc-flash, and reignition risk.
safe_actions: Keep clear of high-voltage components.
Warn others not to touch the vehicle's damaged electrical parts.
Tell responders that the vehicle is electric or hybrid.
unsafe_actions: Do not touch orange high-voltage cables.
Do not touch the battery pack or damaged battery enclosure.
escalation_criteria: Electric or hybrid vehicle involved in crash or fire
knowledge_records.notes: International source; not Indian statutory guidance.

knowledge_records.topic: Electric vehicle battery fire (thermal runaway)
knowledge_records.title:
Do not attempt to extinguish an EV traction battery fire with a portable
extinguisher
knowledge_records.content:
A traction battery fire in an electric vehicle should not be tackled by an
untrained person with a portable extinguisher. These fires require trained fire-service
intervention and can reignite even after visible flames stop.
safe_actions: Evacuate and move far away.
Call 112 and state that an electric vehicle battery is involved.
Keep the area cordoned until responders arrive.
unsafe_actions: Do not attempt to extinguish a traction battery fire with a portable extinguisher.

Do not sit in, re-enter, move, or tow the vehicle yourself after a battery fire or
suspected thermal runaway.
escalation_criteria: Fire or heavy smoke on an electric or hybrid vehicle
Battery pack physically damaged after impact
Reignition or recurring smoke after flames reduce

cross_domain_escalation.condition: Burned EV requires recovery or relocation
cross_domain_escalation.action: Professional recovery only; do not move or tow the vehicle yourself.

knowledge_records.notes: International source; India-specific operational SOPs remain a gap.

knowledge_records.topic: CNG and LPG vehicle fire hazards
knowledge_records.title: A burning CNG or LPG vehicle can vent gas or rupture a cylinder
knowledge_records.content:
When a CNG or LPG vehicle is exposed to fire, cylinder pressure rises
and safety devices may vent gas with a loud hiss or whistle and a long jet flame. If
pressure relief fails, catastrophic cylinder rupture is possible.
safe_actions: Treat a burning gas-fuelled vehicle as extremely dangerous.
Move far away and keep others away.
Call emergency services and clearly state that a CNG or LPG vehicle is involved.
unsafe_actions: Do not approach a gas-fuelled vehicle that is on fire, hissing, or whistling.

knowledge_records.topic: CNG and LPG vehicle fire hazards
knowledge_records.title:
Stay out of the cylinder-end line and avoid low-lying areas if LPG may be
leaking
knowledge_records.content:
People should move away from the line of the cylinder ends, which is the
direction of greatest rupture hazard, and if LPG may be leaking they should also
avoid pits, drains, ditches, and basements because LPG is heavier than air and can
accumulate there.
safe_actions: Move away from the line of the cylinder ends.
Stay upwind.
Avoid low-lying spaces where LPG may collect.
unsafe_actions: Do not shelter in pits, drains, ditches, or basements near a suspected LPG leak.
escalation_criteria: Fire inside enclosed or low-lying space

knowledge_records.topic: CNG and LPG vehicle fire hazards
knowledge_records.title:
Do not attempt to close valves, cool cylinders, or fight a burning gas vehicle
yourself
knowledge_records.content:
Untrained people should not try to close valves, cool cylinders, or fight a
fire involving a burning gas-fuelled vehicle. These actions require trained fire-service
responders and specialised equipment.
safe_actions: Withdraw and wait for the fire service.
Keep bystanders and traffic far back.
unsafe_actions: Do not attempt to close valves.
Do not attempt to cool cylinders.
Do not attempt to fight the fire yourself.
escalation_criteria: Any CNG or LPG vehicle fire

knowledge_records.topic: Trapped occupants and rescue limitations
knowledge_records.title: Call 112 immediately when a person is trapped in a burning vehicle
knowledge_records.content:
A person trapped in a burning vehicle is a life-threatening emergency.
The first action is to call 112 and clearly state that a person is trapped in a burning
vehicle so that fire and rescue services with cutting equipment can be dispatched
immediately.
safe_actions: Call 112 immediately.
State clearly that a person is trapped in a burning vehicle.
Guide arriving responders to the exact location.
unsafe_actions: Do not delay calling while attempting rescue on your own.
escalation_criteria: Unconscious person inside a burning vehicle

knowledge_records.topic: Trapped occupants and rescue limitations
knowledge_records.title:
Only attempt outside-access help such as opening a door or cutting a
reachable seatbelt
knowledge_records.content:
A bystander may attempt assistance only where it can be done from
outside the vehicle without entering flames or heavy smoke, such as opening an
unlocked door, cutting a jammed seatbelt that can be safely reached from outside, or
helping a partially free person out.
safe_actions: Try doors from outside if they are not jammed and flames are not blocking access.
Cut a jammed seatbelt only if it can be reached safely from outside.
Move a partially free person well away from the vehicle.
unsafe_actions: Do not enter flames or heavy smoke to reach the person.
escalation_criteria: Victim cannot be reached safely from outside

knowledge_records.topic: Trapped occupants and rescue limitations
knowledge_records.title:
Do not enter a burning cabin or try to free a person pinned by vehicle
structure
knowledge_records.content:
A bystander must not enter a burning vehicle cabin or try to free a person
pinned by vehicle structure without proper rescue equipment, because these actions
are likely to create additional casualties and require trained fire and rescue
responders.
safe_actions: Wait for rescue crews with proper cutting equipment.
Keep talking to the trapped person if possible from a safe position.
unsafe_actions: Do not enter a burning cabin.
Do not attempt to free a structurally pinned person without rescue equipment.
Do not drag a trapped person forcefully against jammed structure.
escalation_criteria: Fire or heavy smoke inside cabin

cross_domain_escalation.condition: Trapped occupant following a collision with suspected serious injury
cross_domain_escalation.action:
Use road-accident casualty guidance, especially non-movement where
there is no immediate fire threat.

knowledge_records.topic: Smoke inhalation and burn injury response
knowledge_records.title: Move smoke-exposed people to fresh air and get medical help
knowledge_records.content:
Smoke from a burning vehicle contains toxic gases from plastics, foam,
wiring, and fuel. Anyone who has inhaled smoke from a vehicle fire should be moved
into clean fresh air and should receive medical assessment, even if they have no
visible burns.
safe_actions: Move the person into clean fresh air away from the smoke.
Call 112 or 108 for medical help.
Monitor for breathing difficulty, coughing, hoarseness, confusion, or drowsiness.
unsafe_actions: Do not assume a person is unharmed because there are no visible burns.
Do not send someone back into smoke to retrieve items.
escalation_criteria: Confusion, drowsiness, or loss of consciousness

cross_domain_escalation.condition: Smoke inhalation, breathing difficulty, or unconsciousness after a fire
cross_domain_escalation.action: Use first-aid breathing and unconsciousness guidance.

knowledge_records.topic: Smoke inhalation and burn injury response
knowledge_records.title: Cool a thermal burn with cool running water for about 20 minutes
knowledge_records.content:
Standard first aid for a thermal burn from a vehicle fire is to cool the burn
with cool running water for about 20 minutes as soon as possible.
safe_actions: Cool the burn under cool running water for about 20 minutes.
Start cooling as soon as possible.
unsafe_actions: Do not use iced water or ice directly on the burn.
escalation_criteria: Any burn after a vehicle fire

cross_domain_escalation.action: Use first-aid domain for complete burns protocol.

knowledge_records.topic: Smoke inhalation and burn injury response
knowledge_records.title: Remove jewellery and loose clothing unless stuck, then cover loosely
knowledge_records.content:
After cooling a thermal burn, rings, watches, and loose clothing near the
burn should be removed before swelling starts, unless the material is stuck to the
skin, and the burn should then be covered loosely with a clean, non-fluffy cloth or
cling film.
safe_actions: Remove rings, watches, and loose clothing near the burn before swelling starts.
Leave clothing in place if it is stuck to the skin.
Cover the cooled burn loosely with a clean non-fluffy cloth or cling film.
unsafe_actions: Do not pull off clothing stuck to burned skin.
escalation_criteria: Any burn requiring dressing before transport

cross_domain_escalation.action: Use first-aid domain for complete burns guidance.

knowledge_records.topic: Smoke inhalation and burn injury response
knowledge_records.title:
Do not apply ice, oils, butter, toothpaste, ash, or traditional remedies to
burns
knowledge_records.content:
After a vehicle-fire burn, ice, iced water, butter, oil, ghee, toothpaste, ash,
and traditional remedies must not be applied, blisters must not be burst, and stuck
clothing must not be pulled off.
safe_actions: Use cool running water and a clean loose covering instead.
Seek medical help for significant burns.
unsafe_actions: Do not apply ice or iced water.
Do not apply butter, oil, ghee, toothpaste, ash, or traditional remedies.
Do not burst blisters.
Do not pull off stuck clothing.
escalation_criteria: Any facial, hand, foot, genital, or major-joint burn

cross_domain_escalation.action: Use first-aid domain for continued burn management.

knowledge_records.topic: Smoke inhalation and burn injury response
knowledge_records.title: Burn and smoke-inhalation escalation criteria after a vehicle fire
knowledge_records.content:
Urgent medical care is required after a vehicle fire for any smoke
inhalation, coughing, hoarseness, breathing difficulty, soot around the nose or mouth,
burns to the face, hands, feet, genitals, or major joints, burns larger than the person's
palm, deep burns, confusion, drowsiness, or loss of consciousness.
safe_actions: Call 112 or 108 urgently when these signs are present.
Tell the dispatcher that the person has burns, smoke inhalation, or both.
unsafe_actions: Do not delay medical care for facial burns or smoke exposure.
escalation_criteria: Burns to face, hands, feet, genitals, or major joints
Burns larger than the person's palm
Confusion, drowsiness, or loss of consciousness

cross_domain_escalation.condition: Medical first aid and serious breathing problems after a fire
cross_domain_escalation.action:
Use first-aid domain for detailed burn, breathing, and unconsciousness
handling.

knowledge_records.topic: Emergency escalation and Indian fire-service contacts
knowledge_records.title: Call 112 for a vehicle fire in India
knowledge_records.content:
In India, 112 is the integrated emergency number under the Emergency
Response Support System and connects the caller to police, fire and rescue, and
ambulance services. Any vehicle fire should be reported, even if it appears small,
because vehicle fires can escalate quickly and spread to other vehicles or property.
safe_actions: Call 112 from a safe distance for any vehicle fire.
unsafe_actions: Do not delay calling 112 while attempting to search for alternative numbers or fight a large fire.
escalation_criteria: Any active vehicle fire or developing fire situation
